data.name: Blue Planet Diving Center (Dubrovnik — Lokrum & Grebeni wrecks)
data.bestTime: Morning (single boat dive / Discover Scuba slot, back by early afternoon before the airport drop)
data.facilities: PADI 5-Star center, rental gear, boat, warm showers/changing rooms at the hotel; intro dives for non-certified
data.description: PADI 5-Star dive center at Hotel Dubrovnik Palace on the SW tip of the Lapad peninsula — the closest thing to a scuba option anywhere on this route. Half-day boat dives (and a 'Discover Scuba' intro for non-certified divers) to Lokrum's walls/caves, the Grebeni islet reef, Little Africa, and WWII wrecks (Taranto, S57 torpedo boat) ~10min by boat. Fills the trip's complete scuba gap and turns the Day-13 sea finale into a real underwater experience.
data.communityNotes: Travelers consistently rate Dubrovnik's dive centers very highly: the comparable Lapad center Abyss runs 4.8/5 across 242 reviews with reviewers raving about 'the abyss off Lokrum and Little Africa', spotting 'octopi (4!!!), eels, a nudibranch, moray eels, grouper' and a night dive, plus warm showers in the changing rooms and 'passion... intoxicating, focus on safety over sales'. Discover-Scuba intros run ~€90-105pp for 2-3h; certified boat dives to the Taranto wreck are praised as 'a quick 10-minute boat ride'. Blue Planet is the established PADI 5-Star IDC operator at Hotel Dubrovnik Palace with shore, boat and night dives.

data.name: Katun Lokvice (1800m) — working shepherd's katun below Međed
data.description: A high glacial-cirque pasture (~2h on a marked trail up from Crno jezero) where summer shepherds still live and sell cold Nikšićko beer, soft drinks and homemade cheese/kajmak straight from the katun, ringed by Međed, Terzin Bogaz and Bandijerna. It sits directly on the group's planned Black Lake → Veliki Međed ridge route, so it's a natural rest/refuel stop rather than a detour; best June–September.
